Asset: WELL-0074 (SW-24 Well 074, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: flowline Work started: 05 May 2023 08:00 · Finished: 05 May 2023 20:00 · Well stopped for this job: 12 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Daniel Foster Triggered by: inspection INS-0074-0029 on 2023-05-04 Report written: 11 May 2023

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0074-0029 at 14:45 on 2023-05-04 found crude oil on the pad: about 7.7% of the pad area, estimated 2.9 bbl. The inspector noted: "Dark staining on pad." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 2.0 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Thread fatigue from pump jack vibration.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 4 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 2% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 202 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 162 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0074-011

Asset: WELL-0074 (SW-24 Well 074, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 23 Dec 2023 08:00 · Finished: 17 Jan 2024 12:00 · Well stopped for this job: 604 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Kevin Price · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0074-0062 on 2023-12-21 Report written: 18 Jan 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the electric motor driving the pump jack had stopped and would not restart. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0074-0062 showed the wellhead at 6.2 °C with the air at 5.3 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 23 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

Root cause

Winding breakdown from heat and age.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0074-024

Asset: WELL-0074 (SW-24 Well 074, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: downhole pump Work started: 27 Jun 2025 08:00 · Finished: 15 Jul 2025 08:00 · Well stopped for this job: 432 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Brian Coleman · Contractor: Sandstone Rod & Pump Triggered by: inspection INS-0074-0141 on 2025-06-26 Report written: 15 Jul 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that the wellhead was cold and the pump jack was straining with a heavy, uneven load. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0074-0141 showed the wellhead at 41.5 °C with the air at 38.7 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The downhole pump was stuck, most likely from sand or scale. Sandstone Rod & Pump's workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 16 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

A worn plunger that let sand settle and lock the pump.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rods and the insert pump.
  3. Inspected the pump: sand in the barrel and a worn plunger.
  4. Ran in a new insert pump.
  5. Re-spaced the pump and hung the rods back on.

Summary of the fix: pulled and replaced downhole pump.

Testing and return to service

Pump test confirmed fluid to surface and the wellhead warmed back to normal. The well was returned to production.
